editorial.headline: A Lawn-Tennis Club That Remains Open to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: For professional, semi-professional and amateur lawn-tennis clubs, this activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership and remains registrable by a PT PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
A tennis club is not necessarily a venue. This activity covers professional, semi-professional and amateur lawn-tennis organisations or clubs that give members the opportunity to take part in sport. It can apply whether the club provides a place and facilities for the sport or operates without them. The governing idea is membership and participation: an organisation built around access to tennis activity. It is equally within scope where the club’s members are professional, semi-professional or amateur participants.

That breadth matters at registration. At Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, the activity is open. Every stated scale is open, rather than a subset limited to one band. The record is more exact about those permitted scales than about any particular business model. Its stated scope is a lawn-tennis club or organisation giving members an opportunity to participate in sport, with facilities if it provides them and without them if it does not. For a prospective club organiser, the defining elements are tennis, club organisation and member participation.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is plainly open. The record marks the activity TERBUKA and sets the maximum foreign ownership at 100%, so there is no stated national foreign-equity cap below full ownership. The cited national sources are Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. Bali’s status is Open in Bali (high-risk track), and the Besar-scale classification is recorded as Tinggi—high risk. That distinction is decisive because Bali’s permanent provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island.

The practical conclusion is clean: a PT PMA can register this activity in Bali today. It is not a case in which national openness is neutralised by the island-wide moratorium. The reason supplied in the record is specific: its Besar-scale risk position survives because the restriction reaches only Rendah and Menengah Rendah. The record expressly says the activity is registrable by a PT PMA in Bali. For founders, the useful discipline is to read both layers together. Nationally, full foreign ownership is permitted; in Bali, the activity remains registrable because the record places its relevant risk position beyond the moratorium’s blocked bands. That is an affirmative Bali position, while keeping the club’s real-world offer within the stated lawn-tennis membership scope.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, full foreign ownership is permitted; in Bali, the activity remains registrable because its relevant risk position lies beyond the moratorium’s blocked bands.
